person.name: Samuel Akinwumi Adeniji
person.headline: AI for Healthcare · Multimodal Medical AI · Medical Image Analysis
person.bio: I'm an M.S. student in Engineering AI at **Carnegie Mellon University Africa**. I build **vision–language and multimodal models for medical imaging and clinical decision support**. My work focuses on making these models efficient enough to run on large 3D scans, and honest enough about their limits to be trusted in low-resource health settings.

projects.title: ICTC: Instruction-Conditioned Token Compression for 3D CT Vision–Language Models
projects.org: Language and Spatial Laboratories, Carnegie Mellon University
projects.summary: A dual-stage, instruction-conditioned token compressor for 3D chest CT. A Perceiver stage distils each slice and a FiLM-conditioned stage aggregates slices into a fixed budget of visual tokens for a LoRA-adapted language model that writes the radiology report. On CT-RATE validation (3,039 scans): ROUGE-L 0.273, BLEU-4 0.128, RaTEScore 0.801.
projects.summary_plain: A dual-stage, instruction-conditioned token compressor for 3D chest CT. A Perceiver stage distils each slice and a FiLM-conditioned stage aggregates slices into a fixed budget of visual tokens for a LoRA-adapted language model that writes the radiology report. On CT-RATE validation (3,039 scans): ROUGE-L 0.273, BLEU-4 0.128, RaTEScore 0.801.
projects.note: Summer 2026 research internship with Prof. Prasenjit Mitra.
projects.note_plain: Summer 2026 research internship with Prof. Prasenjit Mitra.
bullets: Designed a two-stage token compressor for 3D chest CT report generation. A Perceiver stage condenses each slice to 32 latents, then an instruction-conditioned stage condenses the slices into a fixed budget of visual tokens for a LoRA-adapted language model.
On the CT-RATE validation set (3,039 scans): ROUGE-L 0.273, BLEU-4 0.128 and RaTEScore 0.801 for full report generation.
Built a multi-task instruction pipeline (report generation, entity questions, abnormality question answering) with a 368-test suite, evaluated across six token budgets from 16 to 512.
Now adding instruction-conditioned plane selection, where the clinical question chooses an interpretable, anatomy-aware 3D viewing plane.

projects.title: FPN-Mamba: Linear-Time Bidirectional State Space Feature Pyramids for Small-Lesion Brain MRI Classification
projects.site_status: Accepted · NeurIPS 2026 Africa in AI Workshop
projects.summary: Feature pyramid plus bidirectional Mamba for small brain-metastasis screening on UCSF-BMSR. It outperforms a self-attention baseline (InceptentionNet) on AUC (0.982 vs 0.897) and smallest-lesion recall (0.870 vs 0.788) across 5 seeds × 3 folds, and is 3.7× faster per step than a matched attention mixer at 512 px.
projects.summary_plain: Feature pyramid plus bidirectional Mamba for small brain-metastasis screening on UCSF-BMSR. It outperforms a self-attention baseline (InceptentionNet) on AUC (0.982 vs 0.897) and smallest-lesion recall (0.870 vs 0.788) across 5 seeds × 3 folds, and is 3.7× faster per step than a matched attention mixer at 512 px.
bullets: Combined a feature pyramid network with bidirectional Mamba state-space blocks to detect small brain metastases in MRI, in linear time.

Against a re-implemented InceptentionNet (5 seeds × 3 folds), reaches AUC 0.982 vs 0.897 and smallest-lesion recall 0.870 vs 0.788 (all p < 0.02), and trains 3.7× faster per step than a matched self-attention design at 512 pixels.
Accepted at the Africa in AI Workshop, NeurIPS 2026 — [OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=te52LwNBSf).
bullets_plain: Combined a feature pyramid network with bidirectional Mamba state-space blocks to detect small brain metastases in MRI, in linear time.

Accepted at the Africa in AI Workshop, NeurIPS 2026 — OpenReview.

projects.title: Investigating White Blood Cells as a Source of False-Positive Malaria Parasite Detection in African Blood-Smear Images
projects.readme_title: Where Do Malaria Detector False Positives Come From?
projects.summary: A controlled study of two YOLOv12s detectors on 8,000 thick-smear images from Uganda and Ghana, using seven spatial and statistical analyses. It finds that white blood cells are *not* a systematic source of false positives, which redirects mitigation toward staining variability.
projects.summary_plain: A controlled study of two YOLOv12s detectors on 8,000 thick-smear images from Uganda and Ghana, using seven spatial and statistical analyses. It finds that white blood cells are not a systematic source of false positives, which redirects mitigation toward staining variability.
bullets: Ran a controlled study on 8,000 Giemsa-stained thick blood-smear images from Uganda and Ghana, comparing detectors trained with and without white blood cell labels.

Seven independent spatial and statistical analyses (including Ripley's Cross-K, DBSCAN and Mann–Whitney U) refuted the common belief that white blood cells cause false-positive parasite detections, pointing to staining artefacts instead.
Accepted for oral presentation at the MIRASOL Workshop, MICCAI 2026 — [paper](https://papers.miccai.org/miccai-2026-sat/MIRASOL_018.html) · [arXiv:2609.29663](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29663).

projects.title: Condition-Aware Intensive Care Unit Early-Warning System
projects.summary: Diagnosis-conditioned early-warning models on MIMIC-IV, benchmarking six sequence architectures at 1–3 h horizons. The best model (BiLSTM + attention, ROC-AUC 0.76) is served as a Dockerized FastAPI + WebSocket streaming service, with limitations documented up front.
projects.summary_plain: Diagnosis-conditioned early-warning models on MIMIC-IV, benchmarking six sequence architectures at 1–3 h horizons. The best model (BiLSTM + attention, ROC-AUC 0.76) is served as a Dockerized FastAPI + WebSocket streaming service, with limitations documented up front.
bullets: Benchmarked six diagnosis-conditioned sequence models (LSTM, GRU, TCN, BiLSTM with attention, Transformer, TFT-style) for deterioration risk on MIMIC-IV intensive care data; the best, a BiLSTM with attention, reaches ROC-AUC 0.76.
Deployed it as a Dockerized FastAPI service with WebSocket streaming inference, built for reproducibility under PhysioNet data governance.
